messages:
anya (support): FYI customer @AcmeLabs just opened a support ticket — after the rate policy push a subset of their keys started getting 429s. They say it started ~09:13 UTC. Not seeing obvious billing issues on their account.
micah (eng-platform): ack. Which policy rolled? We pushed rate-policy-v2 (staged) at 09:10 as a canary to 5% traffic. Could be a side effect of the burst/bucket change we added.
tess (eng-sre): can we get the request headers (x-rd-rlimit, x-rd-rusage) from their failing calls? That helps determine if it's quota exhaustion vs enforcement bug.
anya (support): asked customer for sample request/response. They pasted one:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rd-rlimit: 60/minute
x-rd-rusage: 61/60
x-request-id: req_01H4...
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded"}
```
nate (eng-oncall): interesting — rusage 61/60 implies enforcement kicked in. But the policy was supposed to be 120/min for that API key group under v2. Could be misrouting to legacy bucket.
micah (eng-platform): good catch. I just checked rollout logs from deploy-bot: rate-policy-v2 was targeted by attribute "region:global" plus a feature flag that matches header X-Client-Canary. The canary engine picks random sessions; it should not affect key-group mapping. Still, I see a config generation job at 09:09 that wrote burst_window=60s default (we intended 1s). That would reduce effective instantaneous capacity.
tess (eng-sre): if burst_window got set to 60s, token refill math changes — short bursts might be denied. That explains customer seeing 429s even though per-minute looks ok.
micah (eng-platform): repro steps I ran locally:
```
# simulate 10 parallel clients sending 1 req every 0.5s
python tools/simulate_clients.py --clients 10 --interval 0.5 --apikey acme-labs-key
# headers show rusage exceeds rlimit within first 10s when burst_window=60
```
nate (eng-oncall): mitigation options:
- hotfix the config generator to restore burst_window=1s and re-publish configs (fast rollback)
- temporarily remove keys from canary assignment (move AcmeLabs to stable path)
- increase soft limit for their customer (~temporarily) while we fix
micah (eng-platform): I'm going to push a rollback of the canary targeting rule (feature-flag off) and regenerate policy manifests. Rolling that out to the policy-control plane now.
deploy-bot: started config publish job job_id=cfgpub-2026-03-15-0918
micah (eng-platform): done. Published config with burst_window=1s and reverted canary targeting. Canaries for rate-policy-v2 are paused.
tess (eng-sre): I also added a temporary override rule for AcmeLabs api-key that bumps per-minute to 240 until midnight UTC. That will keep them from hitting 429s while we validate.
anya (support): I told the customer we rolled back the canary and added a temporary lift. They asked for timeline for a safe re-roll.
liz (product): we need a clear postmortem entry and to update the rollout checklist: config generator defaults must be explicit and a quick smoke test against a small synthetic workload before canary.
micah (eng-platform): Agreed. Action items:
- micah: patch generator default and add unit test (PR coming)
- tess: run canary smoke harness (10k qps synthetic for 5 minutes) before re-enable
- nate: add an alert rule for mismatch between x-rd-rlimit expected and published policy for any API key (so support sees it earlier)
- anya: follow up with AcmeLabs and close their ticket once they're stable
- liz: own postmortem and checklist update
anya (support): closing loop with customer now. they reported success after the override, no 429s in last 8 minutes. I'll keep monitoring and post final status in 24h.
nate (eng-oncall): one more note — please add to runbook: when a canary touches rate-limit logic, include an automated throttle-sim test and a per-key shadow monitoring hook. We almost missed this until support flagged it.
micah (eng-platform): PR opened: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/5123 (patch default burst_window + test). Planning to re-run canary after test harness additions and a smaller 1% traffic slice.
liz (product): thanks everyone. I'll schedule a quick postmortem sync tom morning 09:30 UTC. :white_check_mark:
anya (support): thanks team. customer satisfied for now. leaving thread open for final postmortem link.
